hints.content:
$g$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals g of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, negative ten and decreases through negative four, negative fifty until it reaches a local minimum at negative two and one-half, negative sixty-five. Then it increases through the point negative one, negative fifty and the y-intercept zero, negative twenty-five. It continues to increases until the local maximum at two and one-half, twelve. Then it decreases through the point four, zero and the point five, negative forty. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative two and one-half and from x equals two and one-half to x equals five.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-5<x<-4$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-2<x<2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is increasing on this interval
$3<x<4$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
